findings.resolution: packages/core/src/canonical.ts now captures Array.prototype.sort, String.prototype.charCodeAt, String.fromCharCode and Uint8Array.prototype.set at module init, replaces Array.prototype.push/pop with direct index-assignment (`arr[arr.length] = v`) and length-truncation (`arr.length = n - 1`), eliminates every for-of iteration in favor of index loops (so Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] is never consulted), replaces PROPERTY_NAME_RE/ARRAY_INDEX_RE/String.replace with inline captured-charCodeAt checks, and invokes all remaining captured methods via capturedReflectApply. Ten new hostile tests in tests/canonical/monkeypatch.test.mjs patch Array.prototype.push, pop, sort, [Symbol.iterator] (including the cycle-rejection path), Uint8Array.prototype.set, String.prototype.charCodeAt, String.prototype.replace, RegExp.prototype.test and String.fromCharCode after import and assert zero hostile invocations together with byte/error-code stability.

npm run compile executed with exit 0 (tsc -b tsconfig.json). npm run boundary executed with exit 0 (`dependency-boundary: OK. 15 workspace packages validated against §14.5.`). Both were run on the exact candidate state alongside npm run lint (exit 0) and npm test (167/167 pass). Recorded in the validation section below.

Recorded BLOCKER-0001 in SPEC_BLOCKERS.md under the §19 protocol. The blocker documents that the accepted baseline (running the repository's own `node --test tests/config/*.test.mjs tests/lint/*.test.mjs tests/boundary/*.test.mjs` on HEAD without the new canonical suite) reports exactly 44 tests, contradicting the acceptance-criterion phrasing '157 pre-existing tests'. The candidate preserves every pre-existing test unmodified (44/44 pass) and adds 123 new focused tests, bringing the full `npm test` total to 167/167 pass. No silent reinterpretation was applied; resolution is deferred to the product owner or a superseding task per §19.

notes_for_reviewer: BLOCKER-0001 was recorded in SPEC_BLOCKERS.md to satisfy REVIEW-003 under the §19 protocol. The blocker does NOT resolve the contradiction; it registers the fact that the accepted baseline contains 44 pre-existing tests (verified command output: `# tests 44 # pass 44`) rather than the 157 stated in the acceptance criterion, so the criterion is impossible as literally written. The candidate preserves every pre-existing test and the full suite still reports 167/167 pass.

Some hostile tests intentionally place assertions OUTSIDE the `runWithPatched` callback (see the `Symbol.iterator` cycle-rejection test). This is necessary because Node's own `assert.ok` reads the caller frame source to build error messages and internally exercises Array iteration when it runs under a patched Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator]; running assertions inside the patched context would fail for reasons unrelated to the encoder. The encoder itself is exercised inside the patched context, and its returned value/thrown error is captured and asserted after restoration.

The captured-intrinsics guarantee now covers: Number.isNaN/isInteger/isFinite/isSafeInteger, Object.is, Array.isArray, Reflect.getPrototypeOf/ownKeys/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/apply, Object/Array/Set prototypes, Set.prototype.forEach, Set.prototype size getter, BigInt.prototype.toString, Number.prototype.toString, Array.prototype.sort, String.prototype.charCodeAt, Uint8Array.prototype.set, String.fromCharCode, util.types.isProxy, and the Uint8Array constructor. Array.prototype.push/pop are avoided entirely via index-assignment and length-truncation. Array-iteration via Symbol.iterator is not used anywhere in the encoder.
payload.summary: Captured every remaining prototype-mutable intrinsic used during traversal (Array.prototype.push/pop/sort/[Symbol.iterator], Uint8Array.prototype.set, String.prototype.charCodeAt/replace/fromCharCode, RegExp.prototype.test) and rewrote the encoder to (a) grow internal arrays by direct index assignment, (b) invoke captured methods only via Reflect.apply, (c) replace RegExp/replace-based path construction with inline character-code checks, and (d) iterate with index-based loops instead of for-of. Added ten focused hostile tests that patch each of these intrinsics post-import and assert zero hostile invocations plus byte/error stability, including a cycle-rejection variant.
